- [`KotlinxSerializationTaskDataSerializer`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-scheduler-db/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.scheduler.db/-kotlinx-serialization-task-data-serializer/index.html): the task data’s JSON
- [`SerializableSchedule`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-scheduler-db/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.scheduler.db/-serializable-schedule/index.html): a schedule stored with the data
- [`dbSchedulerTracing`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-scheduler-db/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.scheduler.db/db-scheduler-tracing.html): a trace for each execution
- [`DbSchedulerTracingOptions`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-scheduler-db/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.scheduler.db/-db-scheduler-tracing-options/index.html): how the DI flavours trace the executions

---

# Telemetry (OpenTelemetry)

Source: https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/index.html

> The application's OpenTelemetry SDK, for traces and metrics, tied to its lifecycle.

`boot-telemetry-otel` gives the application its [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/) SDK, for traces and metrics. `OpenTelemetryService` builds the SDK when it is constructed, so its `openTelemetry` can be handed to instrumentation right away. On shutdown, it exports the spans and metrics still buffered, then shuts the SDK down, so the last interval of telemetry isn’t lost.

The service is in the `Telemetry` phase, the first, so every other service, the database pool included, starts after it and stops before it, and what they record while stopping is in the final export.

By default the SDK pushes traces and metrics over OTLP, to an endpoint you configure. Without a configured endpoint it does nothing. Metrics can still be exposed to Prometheus-compatible scrapers via the [`boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#prometheus) module. The [exporters and integrations](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md) add Prometheus’s scrape, SigNoz, Google Cloud, and a bridge from Micrometer.

## Modules

`boot-telemetry-otel` is the SDK; each exporter or integration depends on it, so an application that uses one needn’t list the SDK. Every module comes in `-kodein`, `-koin`, and `-metro` flavours too, for those wiring styles.

| Module | What it provides |
| --- | --- |
| **SDK: add it, for export over OTLP, or an exporter or integration, which brings it in** |  |
| `boot-telemetry-otel` | `OpenTelemetryService`: the application’s OpenTelemetry SDK, for traces and metrics, pushed over OTLP |
| **Exporters and integrations: optional** |  |
| [`boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#prometheus) | The metrics, for Prometheus to scrape |
| [`boot-telemetry-otel-signoz`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#signoz) | Traces and metrics to SigNoz, over OTLP |
| [`boot-telemetry-otel-gcp`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#gcp) | Google Cloud’s resource attributes, and export to Cloud Trace and Cloud Monitoring over OTLP |
| [`boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#micrometer-bridge) | A Micrometer `MeterRegistry`, for libraries that report only to Micrometer |
| **API: comes with the SDK, and with the modules that trace** |  |
| `boot-telemetry-otel-common` | `withSpan`, `withRootSpan`, and `Sample`, over the OpenTelemetry API alone, for code that traces without depending on the SDK |

## Install

For export over OTLP alone, add the SDK, in the flavour of your wiring style:

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  ksp("org.kodein.di.inara:inara-processor:0.3.0")
}
```

For metrics that Prometheus scrapes, add [`boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#prometheus) instead, which brings in the SDK.

## Configure

The SDK reads `telemetry.sdk`, including its `otlp`, `traces`, and `metrics` subsections. The other telemetry modules each read a section of their own beside it: [`telemetry.prometheus`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#prometheus), [`telemetry.signoz`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#signoz), [`telemetry.gcp`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#gcp), [`telemetry.ktor`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/server.html.md#telemetry) for the server, and [`telemetry.httpClient`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/client.html.md#telemetry) for the client. Every setting is optional.

```hocon
telemetry.sdk {
  serviceName = notes                                   (1)
  serviceInstanceId = ${?POD_NAME}                      (2)
  otlp {
    endpoint = "http://otel-collector:4318"             (3)
    headers { authorization = ${?OTLP_AUTHORIZATION} }  (4)
  }
  traces.sampleRatio = 0.1                              (5)
}
```

- (1) Names the application to every backend, as the resource’s `service.name`.
- (2) Tells this instance apart from the service’s others, as `service.instance.id`, across restarts: unset, each start gets a random one. Set it where the platform has a stable name for the instance, such as a pod’s, from the Kubernetes downward API.
- (3) Turns OTLP export on: without an endpoint, nothing is exported over OTLP. It is the receiver’s base URL, such as a collector’s; each signal goes to its own path under it, `/v1/traces` and `/v1/metrics`, over HTTP with protobuf.
- (4) Authenticates to a hosted backend; take the key from the environment. The headers are `Masked`, so the config report hides them.
- (5) Records a fraction of the traces, from 0 to 1, to cut their volume; by default every trace is recorded. A trace started elsewhere keeps the caller’s decision.

`serviceVersion` and `environment` needn’t be set: unset, they are `build.version`, the key of the build info that [the health endpoints](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/health.html.md#build-info) serve, and `env.environment`, the key [`boot-env`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/environment/index.html.md) reads, so each is set in one place. The others include `resourceAttributes`, `otlp.compression` and `otlp.timeout`, `metrics.interval` (60 seconds) and `metrics.runtime` (the JVM’s runtime metrics, on), `enabled` and `otlp` switches for each signal, `registerGlobal`, and `shutdownTimeout`: see [all the settings](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-telemetry-config/index.html).

### The resource

The resource describes the application to the backend, and is on every span and metric. It starts from the SDK’s default, then `resourceAttributes`, then the typed settings: `serviceName`, `serviceVersion`, `serviceInstanceId`, and `environment`, each winning over what comes before it. A customizer can add to it, as [`boot-telemetry-otel-gcp`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#gcp) does with the platform’s attributes.

### The standard environment variables

OpenTelemetry defines environment variables that platforms and tools set, such as the OpenTelemetry operator for Kubernetes. `telemetryConfig`, which decodes `telemetry.sdk`, falls back to four of them when the corresponding config values are unset: explicit config settings override the standard environment variables.

| Variable | Setting | When both are set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME` | `serviceName` | The setting wins. The variable wins over a `service.name` in `resourceAttributes`, as it does in other SDKs. |
| `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES` | `resourceAttributes` | Merged by key; the setting wins for a key in both. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` | `otlp.endpoint` | The setting wins. |
| `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS` | `otlp.headers` | Merged by name; the setting wins for a header in both. |

The variables take their standard `key1=value1,key2=value2` format, and a variable that is empty, or only whitespace, is treated as unset. A setting from any of the config’s sources is explicit, so a `TELEMETRY_SDK_SERVICENAME` environment variable wins over `OTEL_SERVICE_NAME`. No other `OTEL_*` variable is read, such as `OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER`: set the matching config instead, which a substitution can take from any variable, such as `sampleRatio = ${?TRACES_SAMPLE_RATIO}`.

A `TelemetryConfig` built in code, such as in a test, ignores the variables, so it doesn’t depend on the environment it runs in; `withOtelEnvironment()` applies them to it.

## Wire

The wiring adds `OpenTelemetryService` to the application’s services and hands its `openTelemetry` to whatever records telemetry. It also adds `ServiceStartTracing`, a lifecycle controller that traces the start; see [Trace the start](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/index.html.md#start-tracing).

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
  val telemetry = OpenTelemetryService(telemetryConfig(binder))  // from telemetry.sdk and the OTEL_* variables
  val index = NoteIndex(telemetry.openTelemetry)                 // hand its OpenTelemetry to what records telemetry

  Bootable(
    setOf(
      telemetry,
      // ... and the services that use `index`
    ),
    defaultLifecycleControllers() + ServiceStartTracing(telemetry.openTelemetry),  // the start, as one trace
  )
```

**Kodein:**

`openTelemetryModule` binds the `OpenTelemetry`, and opens the sets of customizers and metrics snapshot providers that the other telemetry modules add to, so import it before them:

```kotlin
fun appDI() = DI {
  import(bootableModule)
  import(hopliteConfigModule)
  import(openTelemetryModule)        // the SDK, from telemetry.sdk, as an OpenTelemetry binding
  import(serviceStartTracingModule)  // the start, as one trace
  // ... and the services that record telemetry, given instance<OpenTelemetry>()
}

fun main() = boot {
  appDI().direct.instance<Bootable>()
}
```

**Koin:**

`openTelemetryModule()` defines the `OpenTelemetry`, over every customizer and metrics snapshot provider definition, such as those the other telemetry modules define:

```kotlin
fun appKoin() = koinApplication {
  modules(
    bootableModule(),
    hopliteConfigModule(),
    openTelemetryModule(),        // the SDK, from telemetry.sdk, as an OpenTelemetry definition
    serviceStartTracingModule(),  // the start, as one trace
    // ... and the services that record telemetry, given get<OpenTelemetry>()
  )
}.koin

fun main() = boot {
  appKoin().get<Bootable>()
}
```

**Metro:**

`boot-telemetry-otel-metro` contributes the `OpenTelemetry` and the service on its own. The start’s tracing isn’t contributed, so that the dependency alone doesn’t change how the application starts; name `ServiceStartTracingBindings` in the graph:

```kotlin
// boot-telemetry-otel-metro contributes the SDK, from telemetry.sdk, as an OpenTelemetry binding; the start's tracing
// is named here, as a binding container
@DependencyGraph(
  TelemetryScope::class,
  additionalScopes = [BootScope::class],
  bindingContainers = [ServiceStartTracingBindings::class],
)
interface TelemetryGraph : BootableGraph

fun main() = boot {
  createGraph<TelemetryGraph>().bootable
}
```

**Inara:**

`openTelemetryModule()` provides the `OpenTelemetry`, and lists the sets of customizers and metrics snapshot providers that the other telemetry modules mark their members as:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface AppModule : ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, ServiceStartTracingModule {
  // ... and the services that record telemetry, given openTelemetry
}

fun appModule() = AppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),              // the SDK, from telemetry.sdk, as the openTelemetry member
  serviceStartTracingModule = serviceStartTracingModule(),  // the start, as one trace
)

fun main() = boot {
  appModule().bootable
}
```

A `kotlin.time.Clock`, if one is given to `OpenTelemetryService` and `ServiceStartTracing`, or bound with Kodein, Koin, or Metro, or given to the Inara modules' builders, is the time of the spans and measurements, such as a fixed clock in a test; otherwise it is `Clock.System`.

When the OpenTelemetry Java agent is attached, it has already built and registered the process’s SDK: `openTelemetry` is then the agent’s, the config and customizers are ignored, and the agent owns the SDK’s lifecycle.

## Push and pull

With push, the application sends its telemetry: the SDK exports spans as they finish, and metrics every `metrics.interval`, over OTLP to `otlp.endpoint`. With pull, the backend fetches it: a scraper, such as Prometheus, fetches the application’s metrics on its own schedule. Traces are always pushed; metrics can be pushed, pulled with [`boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#prometheus), or both.

Pull needs no credentials in the application, and tells the backend when a target is down, because the scrape fails. Push works where nothing can reach the application to scrape it, such as short-lived jobs, or Cloud Run, whose instances have no stable address. The application usually pushes to an OpenTelemetry collector beside it, which batches, retries, and holds the backend’s credentials; some backends take OTLP directly, such as [SigNoz](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#signoz) and [Google Cloud](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#gcp).

- With a pulling backend, such as Prometheus, already in place, let it pull the metrics, and push the traces.
- With a collector, or a hosted backend, push both, and leave Prometheus out.
- Locally, nothing needs to be running: without an endpoint nothing is pushed, and the metrics can still be pulled.

## Spans

`withSpan`, `withRootSpan`, and `Sample` are in `boot-telemetry-otel-common`, which depends only on the OpenTelemetry API, not the SDK, so a library can use them, and leave the SDK to the application. `boot-telemetry-otel` brings it in.

`Tracer.withSpan` runs a suspending block in a new span, a child of the current one, such as a traced server’s request span:

```kotlin
  suspend fun rebuild(ids: List<String>) = tracer.withSpan("notes.rebuild") { span ->
    span.setAttribute("notes.count", ids.size.toLong())
    ids.forEach { index(it) }
  }
```

The span stays current across every thread the block suspends and resumes on, so spans and log events within it belong to its trace. It ends when the block does, with an error status and the exception recorded if the block throws, or a status of `cancelled` if the coroutine is cancelled.

A span from `withSpan` is expected to have a parent. Without one, it starts a trace of its own and logs a warning, once for each span name: usually the caller’s trace context didn’t reach it, such as across a new `CoroutineScope` or a callback from a Java library. To start a trace on purpose, such as for a scheduled job or a consumed message, use `withRootSpan`, which can also link the trace to the operation that kicked it off:

```kotlin
  suspend fun compact() = tracer.withRootSpan("notes.compact", sample = Sample.Always) {
    rebuild(emptyList())  // its span is a child of notes.compact
  }
```

`Sample.Always` samples the trace whatever `sampleRatio` is, for a trace too rare or too valuable to lose; the default, `Sample.BySampler`, leaves it to the sampler.

Log events within a span carry its `trace_id` and `span_id`, which [`boot-logging-log4j2`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/logging/index.html.md)'s layouts print, so a backend can link them to their traces. Logs themselves aren’t exported over OpenTelemetry: the SDK has no logger provider, so ship them with the platform’s log collection.

## Trace the start

`ServiceStartTracing` traces the application’s start as one trace, so its total time, and each service’s share of it, can be seen. The root span, `start application`, begins when `boot` was called, so it covers building the application, such as decoding its config, and ends when the application is running. Under it is a span for each stage before the first service starts, `initialize JVM classes for logging and configuration`, `plan start`, and `initialize`, then one for each service’s start, such as `start FlywayMigrationService`. What a service does as it starts is within its span, such as the queries of a migration.

The start’s trace is always sampled, whatever `sampleRatio` is, so a slow or failed start is never missing. A start that fails records the exception, with an error status, on the service’s span and on the root span.

The span is carried in the coroutine context of the service’s `start`, so it is current on whatever thread the start runs on, including in `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)`, and the coroutines the start runs and waits for inherit it.

## Customize the SDK

For an SDK setting the config doesn’t cover, such as a metric view, a span processor, or another sampler, implement `OpenTelemetryCustomizer`. Each of its methods has a default that changes nothing, so implement only what you need:

```kotlin
/** Buckets of its own for the server's request durations, in seconds: a metric view, which the config doesn't cover. */
object RequestDurationBuckets : OpenTelemetryCustomizer {
  override fun customizeMeterProvider(builder: SdkMeterProviderBuilder) {
    builder.registerView(
      InstrumentSelector.builder().setName("http.server.request.duration").build(),
      View.builder()
        .setAggregation(Aggregation.explicitBucketHistogram(listOf(0.01, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5)))
        .build(),
    )
  }
}
```

They are called as the SDK is built, after the typed settings: `customizeResource`, `customizeSampler`, then, for each OTLP exporter, `exportHeaders` and `customizeSpanExporter` or `customizeMetricExporter`, then `customizeTracerProvider` and `customizeMeterProvider`. For a header computed for each export request, such as an access token, use `exportHeaders` rather than the exporter’s `setHeaders`, which would replace every other customizer’s. This is how the exporters and integrations plug in, too.

`excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(paths)` is a customizer that records no trace for a server request to any of the paths, such as a health check, which would otherwise fill the traces with requests nobody looks at.

**Vanilla:**

Pass the customizers to `OpenTelemetryService`:

```kotlin
  OpenTelemetryService(
    telemetryConfig(binder),
    listOf(
      RequestDurationBuckets,
      excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(setOf("/ping")),  // no trace for these requests
    ),
  )
```

**Kodein:**

Add them to the `Set<OpenTelemetryCustomizer>`, in a module imported after `openTelemetryModule`:

```kotlin
  inBindSet<OpenTelemetryCustomizer> {
    add { singleton { RequestDurationBuckets } }
    add { singleton { excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(setOf("/ping")) } }  // no trace for these requests
  }
```

**Koin:**

Define each as an `OpenTelemetryCustomizer`, with a qualifier of its own, for `openTelemetryModule()` to collect:

```kotlin
single<OpenTelemetryCustomizer>(named<RequestDurationBuckets>()) { RequestDurationBuckets }
single<OpenTelemetryCustomizer>(named("ping")) { excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(setOf("/ping")) }  // no trace for these requests
```

**Metro:**

Contribute them into the `Set<OpenTelemetryCustomizer>`:

```kotlin
  @Provides @IntoSet fun requestDurationBuckets(): OpenTelemetryCustomizer = RequestDurationBuckets

  @Provides @IntoSet  // no trace for these requests
  fun excludePing(): OpenTelemetryCustomizer = excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(setOf("/ping"))
```

**Inara:**

Mark them `@OpenTelemetryCustomizers`, in a module that requires `OpenTelemetryModule`:

```kotlin
@DIModule
interface TelemetryCustomizersModule : @DIModule.Required OpenTelemetryModule {
  @OpenTelemetryCustomizers val requestDurationBuckets: OpenTelemetryCustomizer
  @OpenTelemetryCustomizers val pingExclusion: OpenTelemetryCustomizer
}

fun telemetryCustomizersModule() = TelemetryCustomizersModulePart(
  requestDurationBuckets = Binding.value(RequestDurationBuckets),
  pingExclusion = Binding.single { excludeUrlPathsFromTraces(setOf("/ping")) },  // no trace for these requests
)
```

## Telemetry in other functions

Other functions record through the application’s OpenTelemetry, with `-otel` modules of their own, or with tracing built in, each documented with its function:

- Database: a span for each JDBC statement, in [Database](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/database/index.html.md#telemetry), and the connection pool’s metrics, in [HikariCP](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/database/hikari.html.md#metrics).
- HTTP server: a span and the standard metrics for each request, and the metrics scrape, in [the server](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/server.html.md#telemetry).
- HTTP client: a client span and the standard metrics for each request, in [the client](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/client.html.md#telemetry).
- Background work: a trace for each run of a periodic loop, in [periodic work](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/background/periodic.html.md#telemetry), and for each db-scheduler execution, in [scheduled tasks](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/background/scheduler.html.md#telemetry), built into `boot-periodic` and `boot-scheduler-db`: with Kodein, Koin, or Metro, on whenever the application has an `OpenTelemetry`, and with Inara, through the `OpenTelemetryApiModule` the modules require.

For a library without such a module, hand the application’s `openTelemetry` to the library’s own OpenTelemetry instrumentation, where you build it. For one that reports only to Micrometer, use the [Micrometer bridge](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html.md#micrometer-bridge).

## Example

`examples/server-ktor-db` is a small Ktor server that traces its requests, with a span for each query within them, traces its start, and records its request, pool, and runtime metrics, which it serves for Prometheus at [http://localhost:8001/metrics](http://localhost:8001/metrics). It is wired each of the five ways; from the repository root, run yours:

**Vanilla:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:vanilla:run
```

**Kodein:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:kodein:run
```

**Koin:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:koin:run
```

**Metro:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:metro:run
```

**Inara:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:inara:run
```

Its metrics are pulled, so they need nothing else running; its traces are pushed, so to see them, point `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` at an OpenTelemetry collector or Jaeger. Its README shows how to see both locally, with Grafana or Jaeger in a container.

## Reference

- [`OpenTelemetryService`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-open-telemetry-service/index.html): the SDK’s service
- [`TelemetryConfig`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-telemetry-config/index.html): the settings, decoded by [`telemetryConfig`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/telemetry-config.html)
- [`withOtelEnvironment`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/with-otel-environment.html): the standard environment variables
- [`ServiceStartTracing`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-service-start-tracing/index.html): the start’s trace
- [`withSpan`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-common/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/with-span.html) and [`withRootSpan`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-common/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/with-root-span.html): spans around suspending code
- [`Sample`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-common/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-sample/index.html): how a root span’s trace is sampled
- [`OpenTelemetryCustomizer`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-open-telemetry-customizer/index.html): for what the config doesn’t cover
- [`excludeUrlPathsFromTraces`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/exclude-url-paths-from-traces.html): requests without traces

---

# Exporters and integrations

Source: https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/exporters.html

> Prometheus's scrape, SigNoz, Google Cloud, and a bridge from Micrometer.

Each of these modules plugs into the application’s [OpenTelemetry SDK](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/index.html.md) as an `OpenTelemetryCustomizer`, and reads its own subsection of `telemetry`. Each depends on `boot-telemetry-otel`, so an application lists only the ones it uses. They can be combined, such as Prometheus’s scrape for the metrics alongside OTLP export of the traces to SigNoz.

## Prometheus

`boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus` keeps the application’s metrics for Prometheus, or another scraper, to pull; see [push and pull](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/index.html.md#push-and-pull). `PrometheusTelemetry` registers a metric reader with the SDK, and renders each scrape from it, as a `MetricsSnapshotProvider`, for an HTTP integration to serve.

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-server-http-ktor-otel:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-server-http-ktor-otel-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-server-http-ktor-otel-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-server-http-ktor-otel-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-server-http-ktor-otel-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  ksp("org.kodein.di.inara:inara-processor:0.3.0")
}
```

A scrape is answered in the OpenMetrics text format when the scraper accepts it, as Prometheus does, and otherwise in the Prometheus text format. Exemplars, in the OpenMetrics format, carry the trace and span ids of the measurement they sample, so a metric links to a trace.

### Settings

`PrometheusTelemetryConfig` reads `telemetry.prometheus`; every setting is optional, and keeps the OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter’s default when unset:

```hocon
telemetry.prometheus {
  resourceAttributesAsLabels = [service.name, deployment.environment.name]  (1)
}
```

- (1) Lets queries select series by the application’s own name and environment, copied onto every series as labels; none are by default. Prometheus otherwise identifies the target by its own `job` and `instance` labels.

The others are `targetInfo`, whether the resource is exported as the `target_info` metric, for joining against in queries, and `otelScopeLabels`, whether each series is labelled with the instrumentation scope that recorded it: see [all the settings](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-prometheus-telemetry-config/index.html).

With the metrics pulled, `telemetry.sdk.metrics.otlp = false` keeps them off OTLP while the traces are still pushed.

### Serve the scrape

`KtorTelemetry`, from `boot-server-http-ktor-otel`, serves the scrape at `/metrics` on the application’s server, once the server installs it:

```kotlin
    installTelemetry(telemetry)  // traces each request, and serves the scrape at telemetry.ktor.path
```

With `telemetry.ktor.hostPort` set, such as `":9090"`, the scrape is served on a [listener of its own](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/server.html.md#scrape) instead, which keeps it off a public server: with vanilla wiring, add `KtorTelemetry`'s `listener` to the services either way, since without `hostPort` it does nothing; with a DI, the module adds it, on the engine an engine module’s flavour provides. Scrapes of the application’s server aren’t traced. The server’s other settings are on [the server’s page](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/http/server.html.md#telemetry).

**Vanilla:**

Give `PrometheusTelemetry` to `OpenTelemetryService`, as a customizer, and to `KtorTelemetry`, as the scrape to serve:

```kotlin
  val prometheus = PrometheusTelemetry(binder.config("telemetry.prometheus"))
  val ktorConfig = binder.config<KtorTelemetryConfig>("telemetry.ktor")
  val telemetry = OpenTelemetryService(
    telemetryConfig(binder),
    listOf(prometheus, ktorConfig.excludeScrapeFromTraces()),  // registers its reader; no traces of the scrapes
  )
  val ktorTelemetry = KtorTelemetry(telemetry.openTelemetry, setOf(prometheus), ktorConfig)

  return Bootable(
    setOf(
      telemetry,
      StatusServer(binder.config("server"), ktorTelemetry),  // serves the scrape at /metrics
      ktorTelemetry.listener(CIO),                           // or on a port of its own, with telemetry.ktor.hostPort
    ),
  )
```

**Kodein:**

Import `prometheusTelemetryModule` and `ktorTelemetryModule` after `openTelemetryModule`, and an engine module’s flavour for the scrape’s listener:

```kotlin
  import(openTelemetryModule)
  import(prometheusTelemetryModule)  // registers its reader, and provides the scrape
  import(ktorTelemetryModule)        // KtorTelemetry, which serves it; no traces of the scrapes

  bindConfig<StatusServerConfig>("server")
  bindAppService { singleton { new(::StatusServer) } }                   // serves the scrape at /metrics
  import(ktorServerCioEngineModule)  // or on a port of its own, telemetry.ktor.hostPort, on this engine
```

**Koin:**

Include `prometheusTelemetryModule()` and `ktorTelemetryModule()` with `openTelemetryModule()`, and an engine module’s flavour for the scrape’s listener:

```kotlin
openTelemetryModule(),
prometheusTelemetryModule(),  // registers its reader, and provides the scrape
ktorTelemetryModule(),        // KtorTelemetry, which serves it; no traces of the scrapes
module {
  config<StatusServerConfig>("server")
  single<AppService>(named<StatusServer>()) { StatusServer(get(), get()) }  // serves the scrape at /metrics
},
ktorServerCioEngineModule(),  // or on a port of its own, telemetry.ktor.hostPort, on this engine
```

**Metro:**

The `-metro` modules contribute the reader, the scrape, `KtorTelemetry`, and the scrape’s listener; provide the server:

```kotlin
  // boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus-metro and boot-server-http-ktor-otel-metro contribute the reader, the scrape, and
  // the KtorTelemetry that serves it
  @Provides @IntoSet
  fun statusServer(telemetry: KtorTelemetry): AppService = StatusServer(config("server"), telemetry)  // at /metrics

  // or on a port of its own, telemetry.ktor.hostPort, on the engine boot-server-http-ktor-cio-metro contributes
```

**Inara:**

Compose `prometheusTelemetryModule()` and `ktorTelemetryModule()`, which require `openTelemetryModule()`, and an engine module for the scrape’s listener:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface PrometheusAppModule :
  ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, PrometheusTelemetryModule,
  KtorServerEngineModule, KtorTelemetryModule {
  val statusServerConfig: StatusServerConfig
  @AppServices val statusServer: StatusServer  // serves the scrape at /metrics
}

fun prometheusAppModule() = PrometheusAppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
  prometheusTelemetryModule = prometheusTelemetryModule(),  // registers its reader, and provides the scrape
  ktorTelemetryModule = ktorTelemetryModule(),              // KtorTelemetry, which serves it; no traces of the scrapes
  // or on a port of its own, telemetry.ktor.hostPort, with the listener ktorTelemetryModule adds, on this engine
  ktorServerEngineModule = ktorServerCioEngineModule(),
  statusServerConfig = config("server"),
  statusServer = Binding.single { StatusServer(statusServerConfig, ktorTelemetry) },
)
```

`KtorTelemetry` serves one scrape, so an application has at most one `MetricsSnapshotProvider`.

## SigNoz

[SigNoz](https://signoz.io/) ingests OTLP itself: SigNoz Cloud at `[https://ingest.<region>.signoz.cloud:443](https://ingest.<region>.signoz.cloud:443)`, in its `us`, `eu`, or `in` region, or a self-hosted SigNoz’s collector, on port 4318. Point `telemetry.sdk.otlp.endpoint` there, and `boot-telemetry-otel-signoz`'s `SigNozTelemetry` does the rest:

- It sends the ingestion key, as the `signoz-ingestion-key` header, on export to SigNoz Cloud.
- It sets the resource’s `deployment.environment` too, from `deployment.environment.name`, since SigNoz’s services and environment filters read the older attribute.
- It exports counters and histograms with delta temporality, if you choose it.

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-signoz:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-signoz-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-signoz-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-signoz-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-signoz-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  ksp("org.kodein.di.inara:inara-processor:0.3.0")
}
```

### Settings

`SigNozTelemetryConfig` reads `telemetry.signoz`; every setting is optional:

```hocon
telemetry {
  sdk.otlp.endpoint = "https://ingest.us.signoz.cloud:443"  (1)
  signoz {
    ingestionKey = ${?SIGNOZ_INGESTION_KEY}                 (2)
    temporality = Delta                                     (3)
  }
}
```

- (1) Sends the telemetry to SigNoz Cloud, or to a self-hosted SigNoz’s collector, such as `[http://signoz-otel-collector:4318](http://signoz-otel-collector:4318)`.
- (2) Authenticates to SigNoz Cloud, with the ingestion key from Settings > Ingestion; take it from a secret. A self-hosted SigNoz needs none. Export to SigNoz Cloud without a key fails when the SDK is built, so the application stops at boot rather than failing every export. The key is sent only to a `signoz.cloud` endpoint, so a key set for every environment stays off a local collector.
- (3) Cuts the samples SigNoz stores, as SigNoz suggests, by exporting only what changed since the last export; `Cumulative` is the default. A delta export that fails is lost for good, where a cumulative one is made up by the next. Up-down counters and gauges are always cumulative.

The others are `authenticate`, to send the key whatever the endpoint, or never, and `legacyEnvironmentAttribute`, to stop setting `deployment.environment`: see [all the settings](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-signoz/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-sig-noz-telemetry-config/index.html).

### Wire

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
  OpenTelemetryService(
    telemetryConfig(binder),
    listOf(SigNozTelemetry(binder.config("telemetry.signoz"))),
  )
```

**Kodein:**

Import `sigNozTelemetryModule` after `openTelemetryModule`:

```kotlin
  import(openTelemetryModule)
  import(sigNozTelemetryModule)  // from telemetry.signoz
```

**Koin:**

Include `sigNozTelemetryModule()` with `openTelemetryModule()`:

```kotlin
openTelemetryModule(),
sigNozTelemetryModule(),  // from telemetry.signoz
```

**Metro:**

`boot-telemetry-otel-signoz-metro` contributes `SigNozTelemetry` to the customizers on its own; there is nothing to wire.

**Inara:**

Compose `sigNozTelemetryModule()`, which requires `openTelemetryModule()`:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface SigNozAppModule : ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, SigNozTelemetryModule

fun sigNozAppModule() = SigNozAppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
  sigNozTelemetryModule = sigNozTelemetryModule(),  // from telemetry.signoz
)
```

## Google Cloud

`boot-telemetry-otel-gcp`'s `GcpTelemetry` connects the application’s telemetry to Google Cloud, with no collector:

- It adds the GCP platform’s attributes to the resource, with OpenTelemetry’s GCP resource detector, such as the Cloud Run service and revision, or the GKE cluster, namespace, and pod. Off GCP, nothing is added, and the application’s own attributes win over what is detected.
- It authenticates OTLP export to Google’s OTLP endpoint, `[https://telemetry.googleapis.com](https://telemetry.googleapis.com)`, which writes traces to Cloud Trace and metrics to Cloud Monitoring, with the application default credentials: a fresh access token on each request, and the quota project as `x-goog-user-project`.

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-gcp:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-gcp-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-gcp-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-gcp-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-gcp-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  ksp("org.kodein.di.inara:inara-processor:0.3.0")
}
```

The service account needs the roles to write both, `roles/cloudtrace.agent` and `roles/monitoring.metricWriter`, and the project needs the Telemetry API enabled.

### Settings

`GcpTelemetryConfig` reads `telemetry.gcp`; every setting is optional:

```hocon
telemetry {
  sdk.otlp.endpoint = "https://telemetry.googleapis.com"  (1)
  gcp.projectId = my-project                              (2)
}
```

- (1) Sends traces to Cloud Trace and metrics to Cloud Monitoring, through Google’s OTLP endpoint.
- (2) Bills export to, and checks its quota against, another project than the default: the credentials' quota project, then the project the application runs in.

Export to a `googleapis.com` endpoint is authenticated, and export to a collector isn’t. The credentials are loaded when the SDK is built, only if export is authenticated, so missing credentials stop the application at boot. The others are `authenticate`, to authenticate export whatever the endpoint, or never, and `detectResource`, to leave out the platform’s resource attributes: see [all the settings](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-gcp/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-gcp-telemetry-config/index.html).

### Wire

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
  OpenTelemetryService(
    telemetryConfig(binder),
    listOf(GcpTelemetry(binder.config("telemetry.gcp"))),
  )
```

**Kodein:**

Import `gcpTelemetryModule` after `openTelemetryModule`:

```kotlin
  import(openTelemetryModule)
  import(gcpTelemetryModule)  // from telemetry.gcp
```

**Koin:**

Include `gcpTelemetryModule()` with `openTelemetryModule()`:

```kotlin
openTelemetryModule(),
gcpTelemetryModule(),  // from telemetry.gcp
```

**Metro:**

`boot-telemetry-otel-gcp-metro` contributes `GcpTelemetry` to the customizers on its own; there is nothing to wire.

**Inara:**

Compose `gcpTelemetryModule()`, which requires `openTelemetryModule()`:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface GcpAppModule : ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, GcpTelemetryModule

fun gcpAppModule() = GcpAppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
  gcpTelemetryModule = gcpTelemetryModule(),  // from telemetry.gcp
)
```

## Micrometer bridge

`boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge` is for libraries that report only to Micrometer, such as the Temporal SDK. `openTelemetryMeterRegistry(openTelemetry)` is a Micrometer `MeterRegistry` that records into the application’s OpenTelemetry, so the libraries' meters are exported with the rest of its metrics, with its resource, by whichever exporters the SDK has.

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  implementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  ksp("org.kodein.di.inara:inara-processor:0.3.0")
}
```

It has no settings. The meters keep their Micrometer names and tags; there are no common tags to set, since the resource describes the application. The registry needs no closing: the SDK exports the meters' last values when `OpenTelemetryService` shuts it down.

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
  val registry: MeterRegistry = openTelemetryMeterRegistry(telemetry.openTelemetry)
  // e.g. a library's Micrometer binder: the executor's metrics, exported with the rest
  val executor = ExecutorServiceMetrics.monitor(registry, Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4), "work")
```

**Kodein:**

`micrometerBridgeModule` binds the `MeterRegistry`:

```kotlin
  import(openTelemetryModule)
  import(micrometerBridgeModule)  // a MeterRegistry binding, over the application's OpenTelemetry

  // e.g. a library's Micrometer binder: the executor's metrics, exported with the rest
  bindSingleton<ExecutorService> { ExecutorServiceMetrics.monitor(instance(), Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4), "work") }
```

**Koin:**

`micrometerBridgeModule()` defines the `MeterRegistry`:

```kotlin
openTelemetryModule(),
micrometerBridgeModule(),  // a MeterRegistry definition, over the application's OpenTelemetry
module {
  // e.g. a library's Micrometer binder: the executor's metrics, exported with the rest
  single<ExecutorService> { ExecutorServiceMetrics.monitor(get(), Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4), "work") }
},
```

**Metro:**

`boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-metro` contributes the `MeterRegistry`:

```kotlin
  // boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge-metro contributes the MeterRegistry; e.g. a library's Micrometer binder, the
  // executor's metrics, exported with the rest
  @Provides @SingleIn(TelemetryScope::class)
  fun workExecutor(registry: MeterRegistry): ExecutorService =
    ExecutorServiceMetrics.monitor(registry, Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4), "work")
```

**Inara:**

`micrometerBridgeModule()` provides the `MeterRegistry`:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface MicrometerBridgeAppModule : ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, MicrometerBridgeModule {
  val workExecutor: ExecutorService
}

fun micrometerBridgeAppModule() = MicrometerBridgeAppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
  micrometerBridgeModule = micrometerBridgeModule(),  // a meterRegistry member, over the application's OpenTelemetry
  // e.g. a library's Micrometer binder: the executor's metrics, exported with the rest
  workExecutor = Binding.single {
    ExecutorServiceMetrics.monitor(meterRegistry, Executors.newFixedThreadPool(4), "work")
  },
)
```

## Reference

- [`PrometheusTelemetry`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-prometheus-telemetry/index.html) and [`PrometheusTelemetryConfig`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-prometheus/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-prometheus-telemetry-config/index.html): Prometheus’s scrape
- [`MetricsSnapshotProvider`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-metrics-snapshot-provider/index.html): a scrape, for an HTTP integration to serve
- [`SigNozTelemetry`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-signoz/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-sig-noz-telemetry/index.html) and [`SigNozTelemetryConfig`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-signoz/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-sig-noz-telemetry-config/index.html): SigNoz
- [`GcpTelemetry`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-gcp/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-gcp-telemetry/index.html) and [`GcpTelemetryConfig`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-gcp/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/-gcp-telemetry-config/index.html): Google Cloud
- [`openTelemetryMeterRegistry`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-telemetry-otel-micrometer-bridge/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.telemetry.otel/open-telemetry-meter-registry.html): the Micrometer bridge

# Testing

Source: https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/testing/index.html

> Helpers for unit tests: a test clock, captured logs, start plans, and in-memory telemetry, without booting the application.

`boot-test` and `boot-test-otel` are helpers for unit tests, in plain Kotlin, so JUnit, Kotest, and TestBalloon can all use them. `boot-test` has a test clock, captured logs, a check of the start plan, and config for a test; `boot-test-otel` collects the spans and metrics an OpenTelemetry SDK records, in memory. An application adds them as test dependencies.

They deliberately don’t boot the application.

> **Note:** Bootable won’t add a way to boot the application in tests. Where one exists, as in the Spring Boot ecosystem, it tends to become the way every test is written, because it is the easy way out: nobody has to think about injecting fakes. That makes tests slow and brittle, and replaces unit tests rather than complementing them. If this style of testing makes sense for your project, it is easy to implement yourself.

Instead, a test constructs what it tests, as the wiring does:

- **A class**: construct it, with a fake for each thing it uses.
- **A Ktor server’s routes**: run its module in Ktor’s `testApplication`, with the server constructed the same way.
- **The wiring**: build the application’s graph, or call its vanilla wiring, and check the services it builds and their start plan, without starting anything.

## Modules

| Module | What it provides |
| --- | --- |
| **Test helpers: optional, as test dependencies** |  |
| `boot-test` | Helpers for unit tests, such as a test clock, captured logs, and the start plan, without booting the application |
| `boot-test-otel` | An in-memory OpenTelemetry SDK, to check a component’s spans and metrics |

## Install

Add them as test dependencies, in the flavour of your wiring style:

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test-otel:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test-otel-kodein:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
dependencies {
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test-otel-koin:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Metro:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("dev.zacsweers.metro") version "1.4.5"
}

dependencies {
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test-otel-metro:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
plugins {
  id("com.google.devtools.ksp") version "2.3.13"
}

dependencies {
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
  testImplementation("com.github.rocketraman.bootable:boot-test-otel-inara:3.1.0-SNAPSHOT")
}
```

`boot-test` has no flavours, since nothing in it is wired; `boot-test-otel` has `-kodein`, `-koin`, `-metro`, and `-inara` flavours, for its [module and bindings](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/testing/index.html.md#telemetry).

## Test a class

The examples on this page test this class, which keeps sessions that expire, logs and traces each one it opens, and counts them:

```kotlin
/** Opens sessions that expire after [ttl], logging and tracing each one, and counting them. */
class Sessions(private val clock: Clock, openTelemetry: OpenTelemetry, private val ttl: Duration = 30.minutes) {
  private val log = logger()
  private val tracer = openTelemetry.getTracer("sessions")
  private val opened = openTelemetry.getMeter("sessions").counterBuilder("sessions.opened").build()
  private val sessions = ConcurrentHashMap<String, Session>()

  fun open(user: String): Session {
    val span = tracer.spanBuilder("open session").startSpan()
    try {
      val session = Session("${user}-${sessions.size}", user, clock.now() + ttl)
      sessions[session.id] = session
      opened.add(1)
      log.info { "Opened session ${session.id}" }
      return session
    } finally {
      span.end()
    }
  }

  fun isValid(session: Session): Boolean = clock.now() < session.expiresAt

  /** Forgets the expired sessions. */
  fun reap() {
    sessions.values.removeIf { !isValid(it) }
  }
}
```

The examples are functions a test calls, with Kotlin’s [power-assert](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/power-assert.html).

Construct the class as the wiring does, with a fake for each thing it uses: here a `TestClock`, and OpenTelemetry’s no-op `OpenTelemetry`.

```kotlin
fun sessionsAreValid() {
  // constructed as the wiring constructs it, with a fake for each thing it uses
  val sessions = Sessions(TestClock(), OpenTelemetry.noop())

  val session = sessions.open("ada")
  assert(session.user == "ada")
  assert(sessions.isValid(session))
}
```

### The clock

`TestClock` is a `kotlin.time.Clock` that stands still until the test moves it, with `advanceBy` or `set`. It starts at `TestClock.DEFAULT_START`, 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z, so a test’s times are the same on every run, and it is safe to read and move from any thread.

```kotlin
fun sessionsExpire() {
  val clock = TestClock()  // stands still at TestClock.DEFAULT_START
  val sessions = Sessions(clock, OpenTelemetry.noop(), ttl = 30.minutes)
  val session = sessions.open("ada")

  clock.advanceBy(29.minutes)
  assert(sessions.isValid(session))
  clock.advanceBy(1.minutes)
  assert(!sessions.isValid(session))
}
```

Pass it to whatever takes a `Clock`, such as `OpenTelemetryService`, `ServiceStartTracing`, or `PeriodicAppService`, or, with Kodein, Koin, or Metro, bind it as the `Clock`, which they then take their time from; with Inara, which has no optional bindings, pass it to each module’s builder, such as `openTelemetryModule(clock)`. For a monotonic `TimeSource`, use the standard library’s `kotlin.time.TestTimeSource`.

### Logs

`captureLogs(loggerName) { …​ }` runs the block, and returns the Log4j2 events logged meanwhile to that logger and its descendants, the root logger by default:

```kotlin
fun openingASessionIsLogged() {
  val sessions = Sessions(TestClock(), OpenTelemetry.noop())

  val logs = captureLogs("snippets.testing") {  // the logger, and its descendants
    sessions.open("ada")
  }
  assert(logs.messages(Level.INFO) == listOf("Opened session ada-0"))
  // the one matching event, or an AssertionError that lists what was captured
  val event = logs.single(Level.INFO) { "ada" in it.message.formattedMessage }
  assert(event.loggerName == Sessions::class.qualifiedName)
}
```

The result is a `LogCapture`, closed, with these to assert on:

- `events`: every event captured, in the order they were logged, and `events(level) { …​ }`, those at a level that match.
- `messages(level)`: the formatted messages of the events at a level, or at any level.
- `single(level) { …​ }`: the one event that matches, or an `AssertionError` that lists what was captured.
- `describe()`: what was captured, one event per line, such as for an assertion’s message.

Each event is Log4j2’s own `LogEvent`, copied, with its level, logger, message, thrown, and context data, such as the trace and span ids that `boot-telemetry-otel` puts there. `fields` has the structured fields of a map message, such as a `StringMapMessage`.

A `LogCapture` captures from when it is created until it is closed, so a test can use it around more than one block. It captures what the logger’s level lets through; a `level` lowers the logger’s level while it captures, such as to `Level.DEBUG`, and its other appenders then get those events too:

```kotlin
fun reapingIsQuiet() {
  val sessions = Sessions(TestClock(), OpenTelemetry.noop())
  LogCapture("snippets.testing", level = Level.DEBUG).use { logs ->  // DEBUG too, while it captures
    sessions.reap()
    assert(logs.events.isEmpty()) { logs.describe() }
  }
}
```

Both initialize Bootable’s logging for the test first, with `testLoggingInit()`, as `boot` does for an application: Bootable’s base Log4j2 configuration, merged with the test’s own `log4j2.xml`, if it has one, at the level of `LOGGING_LEVEL`, or `logging.level`, or `INFO`. Unlike `boot`, it leaves standard out and error alone, so the test framework’s output is too. A test that logs without capturing can call `testLoggingInit()` itself; only the first call has any effect. See [Logging (Log4j2)](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/logging/index.html.md) for the configuration it loads.

### Failures in suspending code

A service’s `start` and `shutdown` suspend, so a test that checks that one fails calls it in a coroutine. `runSuspendCatching { …​ }` is `runCatching` for a block that suspends, such as to assert that a service’s start fails. It catches what the block throws, but not the cancellation of the test’s own coroutine, which `runCatching` would swallow, so a cancelled test stops rather than carrying on.

## Test a Ktor server’s routes

Run the server’s module in Ktor’s `testApplication`, from `io.ktor:ktor-server-test-host`, with the server constructed as the wiring constructs it, and its dependencies either fakes or real ones the test starts by hand. The test’s `client` then calls the routes without opening a port. `captureLogs` and `InMemoryTelemetry` work there as anywhere else.

`examples/server-ktor-db` tests its routes this way, against a SQLite database in a temporary directory; see [Example](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/testing/index.html.md#example).

## Test the wiring

A test checks the wiring without starting anything: it builds the services as the application does, and checks which services there are, and their start plan. The application’s wiring is written so that `main` and the test share it:

**Vanilla:**

A class that constructs the services from the config:

```kotlin
/** The application's wiring, which `main` and the tests share. */
class SessionsApp(binder: ConfigBinder, clock: Clock = Clock.System) {
  val telemetry = OpenTelemetryService(telemetryConfig(binder), clock = clock)
  val sessions = Sessions(clock, telemetry.openTelemetry)
  val services: Set<AppService> = setOf(telemetry, SessionReaper(sessions))
}

fun main() = boot {
  Bootable(SessionsApp(hopliteConfigBinder()).services)
}
```

**Kodein:**

A module of the application’s own bindings, and a function that builds the `DI`:

```kotlin
/** The application's own bindings, which `main` and the tests share. */
val sessionsModule by DI.Module {
  bindSingleton { Sessions(instance(), instance()) }
  inBindSet<AppService> { add { singleton { SessionReaper(instance()) } } }
}

fun appDI() = DI {
  import(bootableModule)
  import(hopliteConfigModule)
  import(openTelemetryModule)
  import(sessionsModule)
  bindSingleton<Clock> { Clock.System }
}

fun main() = boot {
  appDI().direct.instance<Bootable>()
}
```

**Koin:**

A module of the application’s own definitions, and a function that builds the Koin application:

```kotlin
/** The application's own definitions, which `main` and the tests share. */
val sessionsModule = module {
  single { Sessions(get(), get()) }
  single<AppService>(named<SessionReaper>()) { SessionReaper(get()) }
}

fun appKoin() = koinApplication {
  modules(
    bootableModule(),
    hopliteConfigModule(),
    openTelemetryModule(),
    sessionsModule,
    module { single<Clock> { Clock.System } },
  )
}.koin

fun main() = boot {
  appKoin().get<Bootable>()
}
```

**Metro:**

A binding container of the application’s own bindings, and the graph:

```kotlin
/** The application's own bindings, which the application's graph and the tests' share. */
@ContributesTo(SessionsScope::class) @BindingContainer
object SessionsBindings {
  @Provides @SingleIn(SessionsScope::class)
  fun sessions(clock: Clock, openTelemetry: OpenTelemetry): Sessions = Sessions(clock, openTelemetry)

  @Provides @IntoSet fun sessionReaper(sessions: Sessions): AppService = SessionReaper(sessions)
}

@DependencyGraph(SessionsScope::class, additionalScopes = [BootScope::class])
interface AppGraph : BootableGraph {
  @Provides fun clock(): Clock = Clock.System
}

fun main() = boot {
  createGraph<AppGraph>().bootable
}
```

**Inara:**

A partial module of the application’s own members, with a builder function, and the composed module:

```kotlin
/** The application's own module, which `main` and the tests share. */
@DIModule
interface SessionsModule : @DIModule.Required OpenTelemetryApiModule {
  val sessions: Sessions
  @AppServices val sessionReaper: SessionReaper
}

/** The clock is a setting: a parameter, which a test passes. */
fun sessionsModule(clock: Clock = Clock.System) = SessionsModulePart(
  sessions = Binding.single { Sessions(clock, openTelemetry) },
  sessionReaper = Binding.single { SessionReaper(sessions) },
)

@DIModule(composed = true)
interface AppModule : ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, SessionsModule

fun appModule() = AppModule(
  configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
  bootableModule = bootableModule(),
  openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
  sessionsModule = sessionsModule(),
)

fun main() = boot {
  appModule().bootable
}
```

The test builds the services the same way:

**Vanilla:**

```kotlin
fun theWiringResolves() {
  // nothing is started: constructing the services is enough
  val services = SessionsApp(hopliteConfigBinder(report = false)).services
  assert(services.map { it::class }.toSet() == setOf(OpenTelemetryService::class, SessionReaper::class))

  checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan ->
    assert(plan.indexOfService<OpenTelemetryService>() < plan.indexOfService<SessionReaper>())
  }
}
```

**Kodein:**

```kotlin
fun theWiringResolves() {
  // nothing is started: resolving the services is enough
  val services = appDI().direct.instance<Set<AppService>>()
  assert(services.map { it::class }.toSet() == setOf(OpenTelemetryService::class, SessionReaper::class))

  checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan ->
    assert(plan.indexOfService<OpenTelemetryService>() < plan.indexOfService<SessionReaper>())
  }
}
```

**Koin:**

```kotlin
fun theWiringResolves() {
  // nothing is started: resolving the services is enough
  val services = appKoin().getAll<AppService>().toSet()
  assert(services.map { it::class }.toSet() == setOf(OpenTelemetryService::class, SessionReaper::class))

  checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan ->
    assert(plan.indexOfService<OpenTelemetryService>() < plan.indexOfService<SessionReaper>())
  }
}
```

**Metro:**

With Metro, the compiler has already checked that the graph is complete; the test checks what it builds.

```kotlin
fun theWiringResolves() {
  // nothing is started: creating the graph is enough, and the compiler has checked it is complete
  val services = createGraph<AppGraph>().appServices
  assert(services.map { it::class }.toSet() == setOf(OpenTelemetryService::class, SessionReaper::class))

  checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan ->
    assert(plan.indexOfService<OpenTelemetryService>() < plan.indexOfService<SessionReaper>())
  }
}
```

**Inara:**

```kotlin
fun theWiringResolves() {
  // nothing is started: building the module is enough, and the compiler has checked it is complete
  val services = appModule().setOfAppServices()
  assert(services.map { it::class }.toSet() == setOf(OpenTelemetryService::class, SessionReaper::class))

  checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan ->
    assert(plan.indexOfService<OpenTelemetryService>() < plan.indexOfService<SessionReaper>())
  }
}
```

The config comes from the test’s resources, as it does for the application. Constructing `OpenTelemetryService` builds the SDK, so a test’s config doesn’t register it as the global `OpenTelemetry`, and leaves out the runtime metrics:

```hocon
telemetry.sdk {
  registerGlobal = false   (1)
  metrics.runtime = false  (2)
}
```

- (1) Keeps each test’s SDK out of the process’s `GlobalOpenTelemetry`, which only the first SDK in a process can be, so a test doesn’t depend on which test ran first.
- (2) Leaves out the JVM’s runtime metrics, which a test doesn’t check.

A test that wires the application with a DI flavour can do without config files: `StaticConfigBinder` is a `ConfigBinder` that the test gives its config sections to, already decoded, by prefix, such as `StaticConfigBinder("health.ktor" to KtorHealthConfig(hostPort = "127.0.0.1:0"))`. Asked for a section it doesn’t have, or for one of another type, it fails, naming the prefix.

### The start plan

`checkShuffledStartPlans(services) { plan → …​ }` computes the services' start plan, the order Bootable would start them in, and runs the check on it, without starting anything. It does so twenty times, by default, each with the ties between services that their orderings leave unordered broken by a different `StartOrder.Tiebreaker.Shuffled`. A service that relies on an order its ordering doesn’t declare fails the check in some of them.

A check that fails is rethrown as an `AssertionError` that names the tiebreaker’s seed and lists the plan, so `startPlan(services, tiebreaker = StartOrder.Tiebreaker.Shuffled(seed))` replays it. `rounds`, `startOrder`, and `random` change how many plans it checks, the start order they follow, and where the seeds come from.

`indexOfService<T>()` is where the first service of type `T` is in a plan, or -1 if there is none.

## Telemetry

`InMemoryTelemetry`, from `boot-test-otel`, collects every span and metric an OpenTelemetry SDK records, in memory, for a test to assert on. It is an `OpenTelemetryCustomizer`: it adds OpenTelemetry’s in-memory span exporter and metric reader to the SDK, whose other exporters still get everything too. Put it in the SDK’s customizers, and keep it to assert on:

**Vanilla:**

Pass it to the `OpenTelemetryService` the class records through:

```kotlin
suspend fun openingASessionIsTracedAndCounted() {
  val telemetry = InMemoryTelemetry()
  val clock = TestClock()
  val otel = OpenTelemetryService(
    TelemetryConfig(registerGlobal = false, metrics = MetricsConfig(runtime = false)),
    listOf(telemetry),  // the in-memory telemetry is one of the SDK's customizers
    clock,
  )
  val sessions = Sessions(clock, otel.openTelemetry)

  sessions.open("ada")
  val span = telemetry.spans("open session").single()
  assert(span.startEpochNanos == clock.now().toEpochMilliseconds() * 1_000_000)
  assert(telemetry.metric("sessions.opened")!!.longSumData.points.single().value == 1L)
  otel.shutdown()
}
```

**Kodein:**

Import `inMemoryTelemetryModule` after `openTelemetryModule`, which opens the customizers' set, and get the `InMemoryTelemetry` from the `DI`:

```kotlin
fun openingASessionIsTracedAndCounted() {
  val di = DI {
    import(bootableModule)
    import(hopliteConfigModule)
    import(openTelemetryModule)
    import(inMemoryTelemetryModule)  // after openTelemetryModule, which opens the customizers' set
    import(sessionsModule)
    bindSingleton<Clock> { TestClock() }
  }.direct
  val telemetry = di.instance<InMemoryTelemetry>()

  di.instance<Sessions>().open("ada")
  assert(telemetry.spans("open session").size == 1)
  assert(telemetry.metric("sessions.opened")!!.longSumData.points.single().value == 1L)
}
```

**Koin:**

Include `inMemoryTelemetryModule()` with `openTelemetryModule()`, which collects every customizer, and get the `InMemoryTelemetry` from Koin:

```kotlin
fun openingASessionIsTracedAndCounted() {
  val koin = koinApplication {
    modules(
      bootableModule(),
      hopliteConfigModule(),
      openTelemetryModule(),
      inMemoryTelemetryModule(),  // its InMemoryTelemetry, one of openTelemetryModule()'s customizers
      sessionsModule,
      module { single<Clock> { TestClock() } },
    )
  }.koin
  val telemetry = koin.get<InMemoryTelemetry>()

  koin.get<Sessions>().open("ada")
  assert(telemetry.spans("open session").size == 1)
  assert(telemetry.metric("sessions.opened")!!.longSumData.points.single().value == 1L)
}
```

**Metro:**

Include `InMemoryTelemetryBindings` through the test graph’s factory, which adds its `telemetry` to the customizers, and keep the `InMemoryTelemetry` you pass it:

```kotlin
/** The application's bindings, with the in-memory telemetry and a clock the test passes in. */
@DependencyGraph(SessionsScope::class, additionalScopes = [BootScope::class])
interface SessionsTestGraph : BootableGraph {
  val sessions: Sessions

  @DependencyGraph.Factory
  fun interface Factory {
    fun create(@Includes telemetry: InMemoryTelemetryBindings, @Provides clock: Clock): SessionsTestGraph
  }
}

fun openingASessionIsTracedAndCounted() {
  val telemetry = InMemoryTelemetry()
  val graph = createGraphFactory<SessionsTestGraph.Factory>().create(InMemoryTelemetryBindings(telemetry), TestClock())

  graph.sessions.open("ada")
  assert(telemetry.spans("open session").size == 1)
  assert(telemetry.metric("sessions.opened")!!.longSumData.points.single().value == 1L)
}
```

**Inara:**

Compose `inMemoryTelemetryModule()`, which marks the `InMemoryTelemetry` as one of the customizers, and read it from the module:

```kotlin
@DIModule(composed = true)
interface SessionsTestModule :
  ConfigModule, BootableModule, OpenTelemetryModule, InMemoryTelemetryModule, SessionsModule

fun openingASessionIsTracedAndCounted() {
  val module = SessionsTestModule(
    configModule = hopliteConfigModule(),
    bootableModule = bootableModule(),
    openTelemetryModule = openTelemetryModule(),
    inMemoryTelemetryModule = inMemoryTelemetryModule(),  // one of the SDK's customizers
    sessionsModule = sessionsModule(clock = TestClock()),
  )
  val telemetry = module.inMemoryTelemetry

  module.sessions.open("ada")
  assert(telemetry.spans("open session").size == 1)
  assert(telemetry.metric("sessions.opened")!!.longSumData.points.single().value == 1L)
}
```

With Kodein, Koin, Metro, and Inara, the SDK’s config comes from the test’s resources, as in [Test the wiring](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/testing/index.html.md#wiring).

- `spans`: the spans that have ended so far, in the order they ended, and `spans(name)`, those with a name.
- `metrics()`: every metric recorded so far, collected now, and `metric(name)`, the one with a name, or null.
- `resetSpans()`: forgets the spans ended so far, such as those of what the test set up, so it sees only its own.
- `spanExporter` and `metricReader`: OpenTelemetry’s in-memory exporter and reader, for anything else.

A `TestClock`, passed to `OpenTelemetryService` or bound as the `Clock`, is the SDK’s clock, so the spans' and measurements' times are the test’s. See [telemetry:index.adoc#customizers](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/telemetry/index.html.md#customizers) for the SDK’s customizers.

## Example

`examples/server-ktor-db` is tested as this page describes, without booting it:

- `common/src/test/kotlin/EntryServerTest.kt` runs the server’s routes in `testApplication`, against a SQLite database in a temporary directory, with the services it needs started by hand, and captures the server’s log with `captureLogs`.
- `vanilla/src/test/kotlin/AppTest.kt` checks the vanilla wiring’s services, and its start plan with `checkShuffledStartPlans`: the seed entries after the migrations, and before the server.
- `kodein/src/test/kotlin/AppTest.kt`, `koin/src/test/kotlin/AppTest.kt`, and `metro/src/test/kotlin/AppTest.kt` check the services that the Kodein `DI`, the Koin application, and the Metro graph build.

From the repository root, run yours:

**Vanilla:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:common:test :examples:server-ktor-db:vanilla:test
```

**Kodein:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:common:test :examples:server-ktor-db:kodein:test
```

**Koin:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:common:test :examples:server-ktor-db:koin:test
```

**Metro:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:common:test :examples:server-ktor-db:metro:test
```

**Inara:**

```shell
./gradlew :examples:server-ktor-db:common:test :examples:server-ktor-db:inara:test
```

## Reference

- [`TestClock`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/-test-clock/index.html): the test clock
- [`captureLogs`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/capture-logs.html): captures what a block logs
- [`LogCapture`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/-log-capture/index.html): captures logs until it is closed
- [`testLoggingInit`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/test-logging-init.html): initializes Bootable’s logging for a test
- [`checkShuffledStartPlans`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/check-shuffled-start-plans.html): checks the start plan under shuffled tiebreakers
- [`runSuspendCatching`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/run-suspend-catching.html): `runCatching`, for suspending code
- [`StaticConfigBinder`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/-static-config-binder/index.html): config sections, already decoded, for a test
- [`InMemoryTelemetry`](https://rocketraman.github.io/bootable/bootable/next/api/boot-test-otel/com.github.rocketraman.bootable.test/-in-memory-telemetry/index.html): the in-memory telemetry
